newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia releases offshore exploration permits.
newsitem.headline: Australia releases offshore exploration permits.

text.p: The Australian government on Monday released 34 new offshore petroleum exploration permits.

"The new acreage released today is made up of 16 areas off the Western Australian coast, seven territories in the area of Ashmore and Cartier Islands, four areas off the Northern Territory coast, four areas off the Victorian coast, two areas off the South Australian coast and one area off the coast of New South Wales," said Resources and Energy Minister Warwick Parer.

"This is likely to be the only release of offshore exploration areas, but I think there is plenty for the industry to chew on," Parer told the Australian Petroleum Production and Exploration Association Ltd (APPEA) conference.
Bids for about half the areas would close in about seven months and the remainder after 11 months, Parer said.
"This will give companies a little more time to properly consider the areas and to put together bidding groups," he said.
All exploration permits would be for initial terms of six years, he added.
The Federal government in June last year released 38 offshore exploration areas, and has already offered some permits from that release.
The government last week awarded nine permits in the Timor Sea, with winners including Shell Oil's Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd, Woodside Petroleum Ltd and Cultus Petroleum.
"We believe that the 1996 bidding round will see nearly A$900 million spent on exploration in these permits over six years, including the drilling of more than 100 exploration wells," Parer said.

In February, the government granted a production licence to the joint venture partners in the Laminaria oilfied in the Timor Sea, near the Australia-Indonesia Zone of Co-operatiuon, earmarked to be the world's largest offshore production platform in terms of production capacity.
"First production is expected in 1999 and could be up to 150,000 barrels a day, which could improve Australia's balance of trade by up to A$1.5 billion a year," Parer said.
Woodside owns 50 percent of the Laminaria joint venture, while Shell Australia and Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd each hold 25 percent. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
